children.text: St. Anthony of Padua Parish Church in the town of Camaligan, Camarines Sur, is a parish church of Franciscan origin that was completed in 1857. It is close to central Naga, so it fits easily into a Visita Iglesia or Holy Week pilgrimage, and it is liveliest during the Kamalig Festival in June.

St. Anthony of Padua Parish Church is a Catholic parish church in the Sto. Domingo area of Camaligan, Camarines Sur. It was once simply called Camaligan Church, and today it belongs to the Vicariate of St. John the Evangelist in the Archdiocese of Cáceres. It is dedicated to St. Anthony of Padua, the town's patron saint. Locally the town name is also spelled "Kamalig," so keep that in mind when searching.
The parish is said to date from
. Franciscan missionaries founded it, and Fray Rafael Benevente is reported to have been appointed its first parish priest. The first church, built of stone and wood, burned down in
, and the present church was completed in

under Fray Juan Ontiveros. One news report quotes the parish priest as saying that, apart from some interior renovations, the original design, foundations, and walls remain. It is counted among the oldest churches in Camarines Sur.

The architectural style is Baroque, most visible in the arches of the doors and windows and in the front facade. The Wikipedia entry lists the building materials as stone, cement, egg whites, bricks made from the ashes of freshwater clam shells, straw, and clay. This was common practice for churches of the Spanish colonial era, and the idea comes to mind when you look closely at the texture of the brick. The statue of St. Anthony stands at the center of the altar retablo, and a newly built belfry can also be seen.
Camaligan covers about
4.7km²

, making it the smallest municipality in Camarines Sur by area and the most densely populated. The 2024 census counted about 25,000 residents. The Bicol River runs through town and the town borders Naga City, so visitors staying in Naga can easily make a half-day trip here. There is no long list of big attractions, but combining the church, a riverside walk, and the town festival makes a satisfying half day. Events in Camaligan center on the church; the plaza in front is quiet on ordinary days, but on the feast day and during Holy Week it becomes a gathering place for townspeople.

The arched doors and windows and the front wall are the face of this church. The texture of brick and plaster looks best by day, and the warm light suits it at dusk. Look at it up close, then step back toward the plaza for a second look at the whole. Also notice the decoration above the arches and the proportions of the window frames.

blocks.title: The statue of St. Anthony and the retablo

children.text: The altar retablo holds a statue of St. Anthony of Padua, the town's patron saint. Avoid taking photos during Mass, and look around quietly when no service is under way. St. Anthony is known as the saint of lost things, and you may see local worshippers coming here to pray.

blocks.title: Holy Week street play "An Dalan nin Pagkamoot"

children.text: This is a Passion play staged in the town's streets around Good Friday. The title means "The Way of Love" in Bikol, and it depicts the suffering, death, and resurrection of Jesus. The date and time change every year, so check the parish announcements.

This traditional Philippine drama tells the story of Mary and Joseph searching for a place to stay. It is described as being held at this church on Christmas Eve, though the format may differ from year to year.
The festival marks the town's founding anniversary and the patron saint's feast day, and runs
June 5–13
(as commonly listed; dates can change each year). The feast day is
June 13
. It draws the biggest crowds, so aim for this period if you want to feel the town's atmosphere.

blocks.title: Santo Domingo Chapel and an old burial ground

children.text: The Sto. Domingo area where the church stands is home to Santo Domingo Chapel, said to be a pre-colonial burial ground and archaeological site. One secondary source links the spot to the church's site as well, but this is an unverified claim, so treat it as background only.

blocks.title: A walk along the Bicol River

children.text: The town has Camaligan River Park, which opened in 2014, a hanging bridge, and a painted wharf called "The Sira." They combine well with the church for a short riverside walk. A river cruise boat that doubles as a floating restaurant, M/B Camaligan, is also mentioned, so check locally whether it is operating.

items.title: Half-day route
items.subtitle: From Naga: church and riverside walk

children.text: Leave your accommodation in central Naga. Take a tricycle or jeepney toward Sto. Domingo in Camaligan, and tell the driver "St. Anthony Church" or "Camaligan Church" to be understood.
In front of the church, look over the facade, the new belfry, and the side walls. Early morning is quiet and the light is soft.
If no Mass is under way, step inside to see the statue of St. Anthony on the retablo. If people are praying, move quietly.
Walk or take a tricycle to the Bicol riverbank and see the river park, the hanging bridge, and the painted wharf.
Have a simple lunch at a town eatery or a street stall, then return to Naga to continue with the basilica and the cathedral.
It is best to visit the church interior outside Mass and event times. Opening hours are not given in official sources, so check the parish Facebook page or similar.
Begin the pilgrimage at Naga Metropolitan Cathedral with prayer and photos.
Move to St. Anthony of Padua Church in Camaligan and look over the building from 1857.
You can continue to Our Lady of the Assumption Church in Canaman, or to churches toward Bula and Pili. A chartered vehicle is easiest if you want to cover them all in one day.
Return to central Naga to rest, then attend an evening Mass or have dinner.
Long-distance buses to Naga run daily from Manila's PITX, Cubao, Pasay, and elsewhere. The distance is about
390km
and the trip takes about
8–10 hours
. Fares are about
depending on the class, and most buses arrive at the Bicol Central Terminal.

Flight routes change often. The direct Manila–Naga flight is reported to have ended in late March 2026. Naga Airport (WNP) has flights from Clark, and you can also fly to Bicol International Airport (DRP, near Legazpi) and continue by van for about
2.5–3 hours
. Check the latest flight schedule before you leave.
PNR Bicol commuter train operations vary by section, so check PNR announcements first.
Camaligan borders Naga City and lies about
2km
in a straight line from Naga Cathedral. The road distance may be longer.
From central Naga, take a tricycle or a jeepney heading toward Camaligan. Fares and routes change, so ask the driver before boarding.
It helps to search Google Maps for "St. Anthony of Padua Parish Church Camaligan" and save the location before you set out.
Camaligan is small, so the church, the riverfront, and the chapel can all be reached comfortably on foot or by tricycle.
In the heat of the day, rest in the shade between stops.

You can visit the church all year, but the impression changes a lot with events and weather. The dry season from December to May has little rain and is good for walking. During the Kamalig Festival on June 5–13 the whole town is in high spirits, and Holy Week and Christmas Eve bring street plays.
Camaligan's average annual temperature is about
, and the Bicol region is rainy for much of the year. From June onward, check rain and typhoon news and keep your schedule flexible.

Camaligan is a small town, so it is more realistic to find most accommodation in neighboring Naga City. Naga has plenty of hotels, guesthouses, and restaurants, and the church is a short tricycle ride away, so staying in Naga and making a day trip is the plan we recommend. Rooms fill up quickly during the Kamalig Festival and Holy Week, so book early.

Eat simply at a town eatery or street stall, and enjoy Bicol cuisine at restaurants in central Naga. Bicol food is famous for dishes made with coconut milk and chili. Opening hours of town eateries can vary, so aim for the lunch hours.

We recommend using Naga as your base. See the Camaligan church and riverfront in the morning, then continue in the afternoon to Naga Cathedral, the Our Lady of Peñafrancia shrine, and a restaurant in town, which keeps travel to a minimum. If you want to eat right in Camaligan, check the town eatery's hours beforehand; if the timing does not work, you can return to Naga to eat.
The church is still in use by worshippers. Modest clothing that covers shoulders and knees is best.
Do not enter during Mass and refrain from taking photos. Check the Mass schedule in the parish announcements.
If you visit during the June Kamalig Festival, check the event schedule in advance and arrive early in the morning.
The dates and times of the Holy Week Passion play and the Christmas Eve events change every year, so check the latest announcements on the parish Facebook page (SAPPCamaligan).
Pairing the visit with the pilgrimage to Our Lady of Peñafrancia in Naga gives you a broader view of Bicol's Catholic faith culture.
It gets very hot, so bring a hat, water, and sunscreen, and carry an umbrella or raincoat in the rainy season.
The town is small and there are few places to spend cash, so carry plenty of small peso notes.
Compare the old parts of the church with the newly built parts to see how much of the 1857 building has been preserved. Ask local residents or church staff politely.
This is an active parish church. During Mass and events, entry and photography for sightseeing may be restricted, so follow local instructions.
Opening hours and Mass times could not be confirmed from official sources. Check the parish announcements before you visit.
The Bicol region is affected by typhoons and flooding. Avoid the riverside walk when heavy rain is falling.
Transport fares and routes change often. Confirm with the driver before boarding.
Motorcycles and tricycles are common on the street in front of the church, so take care when crossing.
Keep your valuables on you, and beware of pickpockets during crowded festival periods.
The central city of the Bicol region, bordering Camaligan, with accommodation, restaurants, and transport connections. It is a short tricycle ride from the church.
The archdiocesan cathedral, about
2km
away in a straight line, makes a natural stop on a Visita Iglesia itinerary.
The largest Marian devotion in Bicol, held in Naga in September. If you time your trip to match, you can see it together with Camaligan.
A chapel in Sta. Salud, Calabanga, about

from Camaligan (the Holy Week pilgrim walk from Naga is also reported as about 13 km). Tourism listings describe it as free and open any time, but it is a private chapel, so check locally outside Holy Week.
